## Correction to the instrument note in this card and in objectui#8504 / objectui#8505 / objectui#8506

Those four cards carry a note from me saying, in effect: *"multi-token free-text queries on this repo's issue search return dead zeros; a single distinctive token works."*

**The second half is too strong and I have now measured a counterexample.**

`search_issues` for `ValueDataSource` — one distinctive CamelCase token, repo-scoped, exactly the shape I recommended — returns **`total_count: 0`**, while objectui#8447's own **title** reads *"`ValueDataSource`'s `$`-dialect matcher waves through every operator it does not recognise…"*.

Index lag is **not** the explanation: `InspectorSelectField` returns 3 hits including objectui#8450, which was filed *later* than #8447.

So the accurate statement is stronger and less convenient:

> **A zero from this repo's issue search is not evidence of absence, whatever the query shape.** A firing lit control proves the index is *reachable*, not that it is *complete*. A non-zero result is usable; a zero is not.

What this changes in practice:

- A dedup section may claim *"searched, found these neighbours, they are distinct"* — that claim rests on results that came back, and stays valid.
- A dedup section may **not** claim *"searched, nothing matching, therefore no duplicate"* on the strength of a zero. Declare it instead, the way objectui#8513 / objectui#8514 / objectui#8515 do, and name a manual check for the triager.

The four cards' own dedup conclusions are unaffected — each was backed by a search that returned results I read (`AiPendingActionsInbox` → 1, `GridSchema` → 13, `HeaderHighlight` → 2, `KanbanImpl` → 1). It is the generalised advice in the note that was wrong, and it is corrected here rather than left to mislead the next triager.

This belongs on this card specifically because this card is the methodology one: it asks someone to census a 41-site population and will be read by whoever writes the eventual lint rule.

## Measured addition to this card's method note: **no single probe in this thread found every carrier** The objectui#8504 dev found a **seventh** carrier of the accessible-name class that three prior censuses missed, and the reason generalises past "widen your regex". I re-measured it on `origin/main` (tests excluded) before writing this. ### The two probes have disjoint blind spots | probe | finds `ObjectGrid.tsx:4362` | finds `AgentPreview.tsx:302` | |---|---|---| | `muted-foreground/50` (instrument 2) | **yes** — this is how the fourth site was found | no — that file uses `text-muted-foreground`, no opacity suffix | | `>—<` (element-agnostic) | **no** — its content is `{t('grid.empty')}`, not a bare em-dash | **yes** | | every `` | ``` packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AgentPreview.tsx:302 if (rows.length === 0) return
—
; ``` `git grep -n '>—<' -- 'packages/*/src/*' 'apps/*/src/*'` returns **10** carriers: ObjectGrid's three (closed by PR #8503), objectui#8504's six, and this one. It does **not** return `ObjectGrid.tsx:4362`, which PR #8503 also fixed. So the two instruments that between them found every carrier each returned a **false zero** on the other's unique hit. ### What this changes for the triage this card asks for The census that partitions the 41 must not be a single grep, however wide. Every instrument in this thread was anchored on something — a class string, an opacity suffix, an element name — and **each anchor's blind spot was invisible from inside that instrument**. A zero is byte-identical to absence in all of them. Run at least three orthogonal probes and reconcile their *differences*, not their union: 1. **element-agnostic content** — `>—<`, and the `{t('…')}`-content variants it cannot see 2. **class-family** — `text-muted-foreground` with and without an opacity suffix 3. **fallback-shaped** — `?? '—'` / `: '—'` with no wrapping element at all (instrument 4's 41) Where two probes disagree about a file, that file is the finding. ### Consequence for the lint rule this card gates A rule written against one anchor inherits that anchor's blind spot and will read as enforced while missing a whole element shape — the precise failure ADR-0049 exists to prevent. Whatever shape the rule takes, it needs a test proving it fires on **all three** of `—`, `
—
`, and a bare `?? '—'`, or it is not the rule it claims to be. Filed for the seventh carrier itself: objectui#8520 (a block-level empty-**collection** state, not an inline missing-**value** placeholder — a genuinely different scope question, which is why it is not a mechanical repeat). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Closed `not_planned` — UI closure batch 5 item 9 · maintainer 「同意」 (chat, director seat summon #29, `session_01EcrTi7s5oDYPHS4Pi7h31d`) 2026-09-24T07:47Z

The card asks for a taxonomy of 41 bare em-dash fallbacks before any lint rule or bulk sweep. Neither will be written. A new gate is default-no at this stage, and the census itself shows the 41 are not one class (option labels, generated markdown cells, duration defaults, paths that never draw). The genuine empty-value placeholder class is being repaired site by site under objectui#8504. A remaining site that renders a bare dash for an empty value is filed as its own defect against that repair. Carrier: objectui#8504 for the placeholder class; otherwise none. Reopening is free.
